newsitem.title: USA: Phila. stands by personal property tax -- paper.
newsitem.headline: Phila. stands by personal property tax -- paper.

text.p: Philadelphia is one of only two governmental entities in Pennsylvania still collecting the personal property tax despite a constitutional challenge, the Philadelphia Inquirer reported Wednesday.

Twenty-four of the state's 67 counties, including Philadelphia, levied the tax in 1996. Most of them have since stopped collecting the tax, fearful that the lawsuit will be successful and force retroactive refunds.
Philadelphia's budget, however, is still counting on about $16 million in the current fiscal year and another $16.5 million in 1998, the paper said.
Clarion County also collects the tax, earning about $233,000 from the resource.

The tax, being challenged by billionaire Walter Annenberg, is levied on the value of stocks of companies not registered in Pennsylvania. A similar tax in North Carolina was struck down by the U.S. Supreme Court as a violation of the constitution's commerce clause.
The Pennsylvania Supreme Court said this week it would decide the Annenberg case.
